'''Hallelujah Picassos''' were/are a [[reggae]], [[Rap music|rap]], [[ska]], [[crossover thrash|thrash]], [[jazz]], [[Pop music|pop]] crossover band from [[Auckland]], [[New Zealand]]. They started life in 1988 as a garage punk band The Rattlesnakes, changing their name to Hallelujah Picassos in 1989. They were released on Pagan Records for their first official single No More, following several self-released cassettes, then with the [[Wildside Records|Wildside]] label for subsequent releases.

New Zealand publication ''Rip It Up'' described their music as a mix and match: "The Picassos mix and match musical styles to keep themselves, as much as their audience, interested. A reggae bassline appears in a thrash number, which breaks to a pop jazz ditty before thrashing back into something with a hardcore bassline which is finished off with a reggae outro." (Rip It Up, May 1992)

2013}}</ref>

In 1991 they were the support act for [[Screamin' Jay Hawkins]] on his two NZ shows.<ref>{{cite web|title=Biography 1990 – 1999|url=http://home.datacomm.ch/mik/ba/h/hawkins_jay/bio/bio19901999.html|access-date=13 November 2012|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070528175238/http://home.datacomm.ch/mik/ba/h/hawkins_jay/bio/bio19901999.html|archivedate=28 May 2007}}</ref> They also played support for Soundgarden, Faith no more, the Violent Femmes, Primus, Beastie Boys, Ice T and Body Count, Asian Dub Foundation, African Head Charge and more. They played at the 1995 Big Day Out, after being overlooked for a slot for the first Big Day Out in NZ the previous year.

In early 1994 they added a fifth member, Gavin Downie, formerly of Colony. After they toured in support of "The Gospel of the DNA Demon" EP in late 1995, Johnnie Pain and Peter McLennan left the band, reportedly for 'spiritual reasons'. After recruiting new members, the band officially broke up in 1996 and occasionally reunited to play live gigs, such as Radio 95BFM's 30th Birthday, in 1999.

Although they had limited commercial success – ''Rewind'' was "the only single that ever made a dent in the charts"<ref name=video>{{cite web|last=McLennan|first=Peter|title=Rewind – Hallelujah Picassos|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JOjYbdU1yoc |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/JOjYbdU1yoc |archive-date=2021-12-15 |url-status=live|via=YouTube|access-date=13 November 2012}}{{cbignore}}</ref>  – the band retains a cult status in the New Zealand music scene among fans who recall their incendiary live shows. They were featured in the book ''Kiwi Rock'', published in 1996.

The band reunited to play live shows in 2013, following the remaster/reissue of their back catalogue on the compilation Rewind The Hateman (2011) and Picasso Core Jukebox (2012),<ref>[https://archive.today/20140917080934/http://cheeseontoast.co.nz/2011/10/14/hallelujah-picassos-retrospective-album-to-be-released/] </ref> featuring their collected cover versions. The band added Darryn Harkness on bass, with John Pain moving to keyboards. They released some new recordings on a four-song digital EP, ''Bullet That Breaks The Key'', in September 2014<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cheeseontoast.co.nz/2014/09/04/hallelujah-picassos-announce-brand-new-ep/|title=HALLELUJAH PICASSOS Announce brand new EP|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304125829/http://cheeseontoast.co.nz/2014/09/04/hallelujah-picassos-announce-brand-new-ep/ |access-date=11 November 2023|archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> Their drummer Bobbylon died on May 25, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://picassocore.blogspot.com/2018/06/bobbylon.html|title=Hallelujah Picassos: Bobbylon|first=Peter|last=Mclennan|website=Picassocore.blogspot.com|date=4 June 2018|access-date=11 November 2023}}</ref>
